title: Minimum Processing Time
summary: Given processors with four cores each, and tasks equal to four times the number of processors, assign tasks to cores such that each core is used once.
statement: Given processors with four cores each, and tasks equal to four times the number of processors, assign tasks to cores such that each core is used once. Use processor availability and task durations to find the minimum time required to complete all tasks.
constraints: There are four tasks per processor and every processor has four one-use cores.
A task finishes at its processor availability time plus its duration.
Assign every task to minimize the latest finishing time.
hints: Only the longest task assigned to each four-core processor determines that processor’s finish.
Sort processors early-to-late and tasks long-to-short, assigning consecutive groups of four.
Pair each early availability with the next four longest remaining tasks and track availability plus the group maximum.
An exchange that pairs a longer task with an earlier processor cannot increase the maximum of the two affected completion times, establishing the opposite-order greedy assignment.
editorial: An exchange that pairs a longer task with an earlier processor cannot increase the maximum of the two affected completion times, establishing the opposite-order greedy assignment.

tests.explanation: Give the four longest tasks to the earlier processor; the latest finish is sixteen.
Pairing the shorter tasks with availability twenty keeps the optimum at twenty-three.
